records.title: Security Incident Update #2 (2026-10-30)
records.summary: Binance states that unauthorized hot-wallet withdrawals beginning around 2026-10-29 20:05 UTC caused approximately $6.3B in token-asset losses. It says it set aside more than $6.34B in company funds, including $5B in the exact impacted token assets (about 80% of the loss), and is buying the remaining relevant assets through market and OTC channels. It reports approximately $3B frozen on-chain, withdrawals temporarily suspended, deposits and unaffected services operational, no evidence wallet private keys were leaked, and additional breach points beyond the initial compromised-laptop hypothesis. Further technical findings were expected within about 48 hours.
records.limitations: Company statement, not an independently audited reserve or recovery report. The $5B and remaining acquisition are not itemized by token; no XRP-specific replenishment amount, trade execution or reserve ratio is disclosed. Frozen assets are not equivalent to recovered assets.

records.title: Binance sets aside over $6.34 billion to cover losses from attack
records.summary: Reuters reports Binance's statement that it reserved more than $6.34B in company funds, including $5B already held in impacted token assets, and that approximately $3B in assets had been frozen with industry partners. Reuters says Binance would verify user funds publicly through proof of reserves.
records.limitations: The reserve and freeze figures are attributed to Binance; this is not an independent audit or token-level XRP reconciliation and overlaps the Binance primary announcement.

records.title: Binance hack drained wallets backing customer assets, reserve data shows
records.summary: CoinDesk's review says the Ethereum hot wallet Binance 14 appears in Binance's 1 October proof-of-reserves address set. It reports that Binance 14 held 1.26B USDT and 89,475 ETH among 37 assets at the snapshot, and that approximately 204,500 ETH was drained from Binance 14 and Binance 16. Given the 1 October 100% ETH reserve ratio, CoinDesk estimates ETH backing would fall near 94% until replenished. It reports 108.26% USDC coverage at the snapshot. It also relays issuer/executive freeze statements: more than 1.567B USDT, around 823M USDC, around 200M in unspecified Ripple-frozen assets and 27M USD1. The next Binance reserve snapshot was expected 1 November.
records.limitations: The PoR wallet discussed is Binance 14 on Ethereum, not any of the five XRPL source wallets. The 94% is a CoinDesk estimate based on the 1 October snapshot and reported ETH loss, not a current audited ratio. Freeze amounts are secondary-reported, chain/token scopes differ and may overlap; Ripple's approximately $200M asset identity is unspecified.

records.title: XRP ETF dashboard through 29 October 2026
records.summary: The dashboard covers five U.S. spot XRP funds through the 29 October session: +$8.4M net flow on 29 October, +$98.9M over 30 sessions and about $1.73B cumulative net inflow since launch. It reports XRPZ/Franklin at +$5.6M on 29 October and Bitwise XRP at about $679.5M cumulative inflow, 38.9% share.
records.limitations: Aggregator coverage is five funds and differs from XRP Insights' six spot funds plus BITW. Flow is not itself a direct observation of all underlying market purchases or secondary-market trading. The 29 October session ended before the first identified Binance XRPL transfer at about 20:05 UTC, so it cannot be a response to that event.

records.title: Ripple and Coinbase Partner to Expand Access to Ripple USD
records.summary: Ripple says RLUSD became available on Coinbase Prime, Coinbase Exchange and Coinbase Retail on 28 October for trading and management, with deposits and withdrawals supported across XRPL, Base and Ethereum. Ripple says RLUSD collateral availability for Coinbase Global Exchange customers will follow, not that it was already live. Ripple says it will provide RLUSD liquidity on Base and reports RLUSD market capitalization above $2.4B at announcement.
records.limitations: Issuer announcement; actual live collateral functionality, usage volumes and XRP collateral amounts were not disclosed. RLUSD distribution is not equivalent to XRP demand; any bridge, DEX, collateral or payment effect requires separate transaction-level evidence.
